+`PipesParser` and `AsyncProcessor` require `plugin-roots` in the JSON config. `PipesForkParser`
+resolves it: an explicit `PipesForkParserConfig.setPluginsDir(Path)`, else a `plugins` directory
+beside the jar or in the working directory. When there is neither, which is the plain Maven case,
+it starts its fork with `-Dtika.plugins.classpath=true` so the file-system plugin it needs comes
+from the classpath, where the `tika-pipes-fork-parser` dependency put it.
+That property is the one deliberate exception. Set on any Tika process, it makes pf4j also
+accept factories found through `META-INF/extensions.idx` on the classpath, running in the
+application classloader with none of the plugin isolation; a zip in `plugin-roots` still wins over
+a classpath copy of the same plugin. It is there for embedding, not for installing plugins, and
+what happens on a classpath assembled that way is yours to own.
